concerns.text: T012.5 (select_top_species) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T011 (download_ebd) and T011.1 (download_ebd_fallback) to exist before it can filter species. A task that reads an artifact produced by another task cannot be parallel-safe with the producer. The [P] tag is incorrect and creates a race condition risk.

T013 (merge_and_buffer) is marked [P] but depends on T012.5, T012, T012.1, and T008b. It consumes artifacts from multiple upstream tasks. Marking it [P] implies it can run in parallel with its producers, which is impossible. The [P] tag must be removed.

T019 (train.py) is marked [P] but depends on T016 (aggregate.py). The task description explicitly states it loads `data/processed/species_profiles.csv` (from T016). A consumer task cannot be parallel-safe with its producer. The [P] tag is invalid.

T020 (evaluate.py) is marked [P] but depends on T019 (train.py) to load the trained model. The task description confirms this dependency. Marking it [P] is a semantic violation of the producer-consumer rule.

T025 (plot_confusion.py) is marked [P] but depends on T012.5, T019, T020, and T021. It consumes the model and evaluation results. It cannot run in parallel with its producers. The [P] tag is incorrect.
T026 (plot_importance.py) is marked [P] but depends on T019, T020, and T021. It consumes model outputs. The [P] tag is invalid.

T027a (map_habitat.py Part A) is marked [P] but depends on T019 (model training). It applies the trained model to a spatial grid. It cannot run in parallel with the training task. The [P] tag is invalid.
T027b (map_habitat.py Part B) is marked [P] but depends on T027a. It iterates over species using the output of Part A. It cannot be parallel-safe with its immediate producer.
T027c (map_habitat.py Part C) is marked [P] but depends on T027b. It validates the output of Part B. It cannot be parallel-safe with its immediate producer.
T028 (generate report) is marked [P] but depends on T019, T020, T021. It consumes model metrics. The [P] tag is invalid.
T028.5 (validate_importance) is marked [P] but depends on T028 (report generation) and the model outputs. It cannot run in parallel with its producers. The [P] tag is invalid.
T015 (validate_schema) is marked [P] but depends on T013 (merge_and_buffer). It validates the output of T013. It cannot be parallel-safe with its producer.
T010 (validate schema compliance) is marked [P] but depends on T013. It validates the output of T013. It cannot be parallel-safe with its producer.
T016 (aggregate) is marked [P] but depends on T013. It aggregates the output of T013. It cannot be parallel-safe with its producer.
T018 (unit test for metrics) is marked [P] but depends on T020. It tests the output of T020. It cannot be parallel-safe with its producer.
T023 (integration test) is marked [P] but depends on T019 and T020. It tests the integration of these tasks. It cannot be parallel-safe with its producers.
T035 (validate resources) is marked [P] but depends on T005 and T007.5. It measures the runtime of T007.5. It cannot be parallel-safe with its producer.

T007.5 (orchestration script) is marked [P] but depends on the implementation of downstream scripts (T011, T012, etc.). While the skeleton can be written early, the task description implies full functionality depends on downstream tasks. If the task is to 'implement' the full script, it cannot be parallel-safe with the scripts it orchestrates. If it is only the skeleton, the description is misleading. Given the 'CRITICAL' note about dependencies, the [P] tag is likely incorrect for the full implementation intent.

T006a and T006b (test stubs) are marked [P]. While creating stubs can be parallel, the task description for T006a mentions 'verify pytest returns exit code 1', which implies running the test. If the test runs, it depends on the code being tested (which may not exist yet). If it's just creating the file, [P] is okay, but the description is ambiguous. However, the bigger issue is T006a depends on T004 (config) and T005 (provenance) implicitly if the tests import them. The [P] tag might be risky if the tests import shared modules.

T004 (config) and T005 (provenance) are marked [P]. These are foundational tasks. While they can be written in parallel, T005 (provenance) likely depends on T004 (config) for paths. If T005 imports T004, they are not parallel-safe. The [P] tag is risky.
